goal: Locate single-month volume anomalies in offline_data/regional_sales.csv by computing each region×product_line monthly volume as a multiple of its own 24-month mean, report the top-3 combos with their multiples and return rates, judge whether the spike is real demand or channel stuffing, and save a fully-sourced Markdown report to disk.

plan.title: Inspect CSV structure: Read offline_data/regional_sales.csv: list all column names, total row count, date range (min/max of the month column), unique regions, unique product lines, and print first 5 rows as sample

Compute monthly volume anomaly ratios: Using the CSV, for each (region × product_line) compute the 24-month rolling mean of monthly sales volume, then compute the ratio = current_month_volume / 24-month_mean for every month. Save the full result table to a CSV file (e.g. offline_data/volume_anomaly_ratios.csv) with columns: region, product_line, month, monthly_volume, mean_24m, ratio

Identify top-3 anomaly combos & fetch return rates: From the saved ratios CSV, find the top-3 (region, product_line, month) by ratio. For each, also extract the return_rate (or equivalent column) for that same region×product_line×month from the original CSV. Save a small summary CSV (offline_data/top3_anomalies.csv) with columns: rank, region, product_line, month, monthly_volume, mean_24m, ratio, return_rate

Assess demand vs channel stuffing: For each of the top-3 combos, compute supporting signals from the CSV: (a) return_rate level, (b) whether the spike is a single-month spike or sustained (compare with adjacent months' ratios), (c) whether other regions/product lines show similar spikes in the same month (cross-sectional check). Save a signal summary CSV (offline_data/stuffing_signals.csv)

Write Markdown report with embedded data: Write a comprehensive Markdown report to offline_data/volume_anomaly_report.md. Requirements: (1) H1 title; (2) at least one data table showing the top-3 combos with all key numbers; (3) every key number annotated with source in the format '（来源：offline_data/regional_sales.csv 的 <列名>，<聚合口径与样本行数>）' or '（来源：由前述两行计算）'; (4) a concluding paragraph judging whether each spike is more likely real demand or channel stuffing, citing the signals; (5) no external data — all from the local CSV only. Embed the data tables directly in the Markdown (no separate chart files needed since the user did not request charts)
